questions.q: What does "non-custodial" mean for a DeFi protocol?
options: The protocol never takes control of your asset — you sign every transaction yourself
The protocol requires users to pass KYC before depositing
The protocol custom-builds a wallet for every new user
The protocol is run by a custodian bank on behalf of users
questions.explain: Non-custodial means your wallet holds the asset directly; the contract can only execute what its code says when you call it, not take control of funds.

questions.q: Why couldn't a self-custodial protocol freeze a user's wallet the way a centralized exchange froze withdrawals during the FTX collapse?
options: Self-custodial protocols always have a government guarantee against freezes
There's no account or company in the loop — the user's wallet holds the asset directly, not a company-controlled balance
Self-custodial protocols are required by law to never pause anything
Centralized exchanges and DeFi protocols work identically under the hood
questions.explain: FTX could freeze withdrawals because it held custody of user assets. A self-custodial protocol has no custody to revoke in the first place.

questions.q: Which of the four pillars means "no application or approval process gates who can use the protocol"?
options: Transparent
Composable
Permissionless
Non-custodial
questions.explain: Permissionless means anyone with a wallet can call the contract directly — no allowlist, no geographic gate, no approval queue.

questions.q: Why is "trust-minimized" a more accurate description than "trustless"?
options: Because DeFi protocols actually require more trust than banks do
Because "trustless" and "trust-minimized" mean exactly the same thing
Because DeFi protocols are legally required to use the word "trust-minimized"
Because users still trust the code has no critical bug, the oracle isn't manipulated, and no admin key can drain funds
questions.explain: DeFi relocates trust from a company's legal promises to a smart contract's verifiable logic — it doesn't eliminate the need to trust something.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what has happened even to audited DeFi protocols?
options: They have still been exploited for hundreds of millions of dollars
They have never experienced any loss of funds
They are legally immune from smart contract bugs
Audits make exploits mathematically impossible
questions.explain: An audit reduces risk but doesn't eliminate it — audited protocols have still suffered large exploits, which is why evaluating risk matters throughout this course.
